It is under the ownership of the [[Government of India]] and under administrative control of the [[Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways]], with its headquarters in [[Mumbai]].{{cite web|url=http://www.shipindia.com/newsite/DisplayContent.asp?CategoryID=1&ContentID=50|title=Contact Us - Registered Office: Shipping House|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081210140743/http://www.shipindia.com/newsite/DisplayContent.asp?CategoryID=1&ContentID=50|archive-date=10 December 2008}} ==History== [[File:SCI HQ.jpg|left|thumb|The headquarters of the Shipping Corporation of India at the [[Nariman Point]], [[Mumbai]]]] SCI was established on 2 October 1961 by the [[Consolidation (business)|amalgamation]] of Eastern Shipping Corporation and Western Shipping Corporation. Two more shipping companies, Jayanti Shipping Company and Mogul Lines Limited, were merged with SCI in 1973 and 1986, respectively.{{Cite web|url=http://www.shipindia.com/newsite/DisplayContent.asp?ContentID=1|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20091215204010/http://www.shipindia.com/newsite/DisplayContent.asp?ContentID=1|url-status=dead|title=About us: Shipping Corporation of India|archivedate=15 December 2009}} SCI started with 19 [[ship|vessels]]. It gradually metamorphosed into a [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] having 80 ships of 59 [[lakh]] (5.9 million) tonnes deadweight (DWT) with interests in different segments of the shipping trade. The fleet size of the merchant carrier had peaked at over 120 vessels which included liners, [[oil tankers]], [[gas carriers]], [[chemical tankers]], [[Passenger ship|passenger vessels]], [[Offshore supply vessel|offshore vessels]].{{Cite news|title=Why is the Govt. reviving a PSU?|url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/why-is-the-govt-reviving-a-psu/article70338529.ece|work=The Hindu|date=2025-11-30|access-date=2025-12-02|issn=0971-751X|language=en-IN|first=M.|last=Kalyanaraman}} Inland & Coastal Shipping Ltd. (ICSL), SCI's wholly owned subsidiary, was incorporated in 2016 after the Maritime India summit for undertaking/providing transport services through Inland waterways and coastal shipping.{{Citation needed|date=May 2025}} In year 2003, the company recruited their first ever girls batch, the batch TNOC35 had 3 girls Namrata Singh Tarkar, Anuradha Jha and Suneha Gadpande and rest 32 boys.{{Citation needed|date=December 2025}} SCI has a fleet of 55 vessels as of August 2025. == Fleet expansion == [[File:Path to caves, Gharapuri, Maharashtra 400094, India - panoramio (14).jpg|thumb|Maharshi Parashuram ship built in 2002 by the [[Cochin Shipyard]] for SCI]] On 21 November 2019, the [[Government of India]] approved the privatisation of SCI.{{cite web|author=Arup Roychoudhury |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/privatisation-push-cabinet-approves-strategic-sale-of-bpcl-4-other-psus-119112100076_1.html |title=Privatisation push: Cabinet approves strategic sale of BPCL, 4 other PSUs | Business Standard News |work=Business Standard|date=21 November 2019 |access-date=2020-05-13}} In 2022, the privatisation was delayed by the [[Russo-Ukrainian War|Russo-Ukraine war]].{{Cite news |last1=Saxena |first1=Ragini |last2=Amin |first2=Haslinda |last3=Salamat |first3=Rishaad |date=8 March 2022 |title=Ukraine war a roadblock for SCI privatisation |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/ukraine-war-a-roadblock-for-sci-privatisation/articleshow/90073629.cms |access-date=2022-05-07}} However, the privatisation of SCI did not go through as the government announced in May 2025 that the national merchant carrier would buy over 200 vessels of all types by forming a joint venture of the respective stakeholder, mostly State-owned. This included the procurement 112 tankers at a cost of {{INRConvert|85000|c|lk=on|year=2025}} through 2047. Of this, 79 vessels, including 30 medium-range ones, would be bought in the first phase. The initiative will support India's plans to expand [[oil refinery]] annual capacity from the current 250 million tons to 450 million tons by 2030. Simultaneously, it will also expand the indigenous tankers in the Indian fleet from 5% in 2025 to 7% in 2030 and 69% by 2047. The first order for 10 ships is expected to be issued in May itself.{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/industry/news/india-to-invest-10-billion-in-homegrown-oil-tanker-fleet-by-2040-125052001839_1.html|title=India to invest $10 billion in homegrown oil tanker fleet by 2040|date=2025-05-20|access-date=2025-12-02|work=[[Business Standard]]}}{{Cite web|title=How India’s plan to build 112 crude oil tankers is a bold move for energy security, self-reliance|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india-today-insight/story/how-indias-plan-to-build-112-crude-oil-tankers-is-a-bold-move-for-energy-security-self-reliance-2730755-2025-05-26|website=India Today|date=2025-05-26|access-date=2025-12-02|language=en|first=Anilesh S.|last=Mahajan}}{{Cite news|title=India plans massive $10 billion purchase of ‘over 100 Make in India’ crude oil tankers|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/india-plans-massive-10-billion-purchase-of-over-100-make-in-india-crude-oil-tankers/articleshow/121311439.cms|work=The Times of India|date=2025-05-21|access-date=2025-12-02|issn=0971-8257}} In August 2025, SCI was planning to purchase 26 vessels at a cost of {{INRConvert|19820|c|lk=|year=2025}}. This will have a cumulative internal volume of 1.18 million gross tonnes. Overall, the firm plans to buy 207 vessels at {{INRConvert|1.5|t|lk=|year=2025}}.{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/state-run-shipping-corp-of-india-to-buy-26-local-vessels-in-2-bn-deal-125081100939_1.html|title=State-run Shipping Corp of India to buy 26 local vessels in $2 bn deal|date=2025-08-11|access-date=2025-12-02|work=[[Business Standard]]}}{{Cite news|title=Shipping Corporation of India to buy local vessels in $2 billion deal|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/shipping-/-transport/shipping-corporation-of-india-to-buy-local-vessels-in-2-billion-deal/articleshow/123232961.cms|work=The Economic Times|date=2025-08-11|access-date=2025-12-02|issn=0013-0389|first=Mihir|last=Mishra}} === Very Large Gas Carriers === In January 2026, SCI issued an [[Expression of Interest]] to acquire 8 [[Gas carrier|Very Large Gas Carriers]] (VLGC). Under the project, up to two ships can be delivered by an international shipyard, and the rest of 6 will be delivered by a local shipyard. The International shipyard must have experience of delivering at least 3 ships of the same class, VLGC, [[LNG carrier|LNGC]], or [[LEG carrier|VLEC]], in the past 5 years and should explain their plans for local collaboration for the latter 6 ships. Further, a bigger from a country sharing a land border with India must be registered with the Competent Authority to be eligible. The Press 3 Note is also applicable in order to keep a check on Chinese investments and participation.{{Cite news |last=Mishra |first=Twesh |date=2026-01-26 |title=Shipping Corporation of India seeks to acquire eight new very large gas carriers |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/shipping-/-transport/shipping-corporation-of-india-seeks-to-acquire-eight-new-very-large-gas-carriers/articleshow/127552563.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2026-01-29 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} [[Swan Defence and Heavy Industries Limited|Swan Defence and Heavy Industries]] (SDHI) has partnered with [[Samsung Heavy Industries]] for the contract. The ships will be owned by a planned [[joint venture]] of SCI and four state-owned oil firms.{{Cite web |last= |date=2026-04-07 |title=SDHI wins India’s first ammonia dual-fuel bulk carrier order worth over ₹2,600 crore |url=https://infra.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/ports-shipping/sdhi-wins-indias-first-ammonia-dual-fuel-bulk-carrier-order-worth-over-2600-crore/130074124 |access-date=2026-04-07 |website=ETInfra.com |language=en}} === Medium-range product tanker === As of 23 February 2026, the carrier has floated a [[Invitation to tender|tender]] for a firm order of two [[Marine LNG Engine|dual-fuel]], [[Oil tanker#Size categories|Medium Range Product Tanker]] for $200 million along with an [[Option contract|option]] for two further vessels. An initial bid has been submitted by [[Cochin Shipyard Limited]] (CSL), Swan Defence and Heavy Industries (SDHI), [[L&T Shipbuilding]] ([[Kattupalli Shipyard]]) and a [[consortium]] of [[Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers]] (GRSE) and [[Hindustan Shipyard Limited]] (HSL). While GRSE and HSL have formed a consortium, CSL, SDHI and L&T has formed an alliance with [[HD Hyundai Heavy Industries|HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering]], Samsung Heavy Industries and [[Hanwha Ocean]], respectively, for the project. All of these allies are based in [[South Korea]]. L&T has also sought support from [[Seoul]]-based KmsEmec Co. Ltd., a ship designing firm. This is a maiden attempt to construct a locally grown tanker in decades.{{Cite web |last= |date=23 February 2026 |title=Cochin Shipyard, SDHI, L&T and GRSE-HSL team file bids to build M R tankers for oil PSUs |url=https://infra.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/ports-shipping/cochin-shipyard-sdhi-lt-and-grse-hsl-team-file-bids-to-build-m-r-tankers-for-oil-psus/128702234 |access-date=24 February 2026 |website=ETInfra.com |language=en}} === Platform supply vessel === On 18 March 2026, SCI signed a shipbuilding contract with the [[Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders]] to acquire one 3,000 [[deadweight tonnage]] (DWT) methanol dual-fuel [[platform supply vessel]]. This is the first [[green fuel]] ship to be acquired by the firm.{{Cite web |last= |date=2026-03-18 |title=Shipping Corporation of India signs contract with Mazagon Dock for methanol-powered supply vessel |url=https://infra.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/ports-shipping/shipping-corporation-of-india-signs-contract-with-mazagon-dock-for-methanol-powered-supply-vessel/129653867 |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=ETInfra.com |language=en}} === Feeder container ships === On 26 April 2026, SCI officially launched a [[invitation to tender]] from shipyards to acquire acquire six methanol dual-fuel [[Feeder ship|feeder]] [[container ships]], each having a capacity to carry 1,700 [[twenty-foot equivalent units]] (TEUs) — at a cost of around $360 million. The contract will include two firm and four options ships. The local shipyards will have a "Right of First Refusal" (RoFR) to meet the lowest bid by a foreign shipyard and win the contract.{{Cite web |last=Manoj |first=P |date=2026-04-26 |title=SCI floats tender to construct 6 methanol dual fuel ready container ships locally in $360 mn deal |url=https://infra.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/ports-shipping/shipping-corporation-of-india-invites-bids-for-360-million-methanol-dual-fuel-container-ships/130526513 |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=ETInfra.com |language=en}} === Cellular container ships === On 3 August 2026, SCI launched another tender for a contract of building two firm and four optional [[Cellular vessel|cellular container ships]] each with a capacity of 8,000 [[twenty-foot equivalent units]] (TEUs) at a cost of around $720 million. The tender will also have the RoFR feature for an advantage to local shipyards.{{Cite web |last=Manoj |first=P. |date=2026-08-03 |title=SCI floats global tender to build 6 cellular container ships of 8,000 TEU capacity worth $720 million |url=https://infra.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/ports-shipping/shipping-corporation-of-india-launches-720-million-global-tender-for-6-new-cellular-container-ships/132817012 |access-date=2026-08-03 |website=ETInfra.com |language=en}} ==Services== * Cruise liner and Passenger services * Bulk carrier and tanker services * Offshore services ==Major clients== * [[Bharat Heavy Electricals]] * [[Bharat Petroleum]] * [[BP]] * [[British Gas]] * [[Geological Survey of India]] * [[Hindustan Petroleum]] * [[Indian Oil Corporation]] * [[Oil & Natural Gas Corporation]] * [[Reliance Industries]] * [[Royal Dutch Shell|Shell]] * [[Steel Authority of India]] * [[Taj Cruises]] * [[Tata Group|Tata tea]] ==See also== {{portal | India }} * [[Borders of India]] * [[Container Corporation of India]] * [[Coastal India]] * [[Exclusive economic zone of India]] * First girl batch in 2003: Namrata Singh Tarkar,Suneha Gadpande, and Anuradha Jha * [[Fishing in India]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{Transport in India}} {{Public Sector Undertakings in India}} {{authority control}} [[Category:Companies based in Mumbai]] [[Category:Container shipping companies]] [[Category:Shipping companies of India]] [[Category:Transport companies established in 1961]] [[Category:Gas shipping companies]] [[Category:Government-owned companies of India]] [[Category:1961 establishments in Maharashtra]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1961]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]
extract: The Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) is an Indian  public sector undertaking  that operates and manages vessels servicing both national and international lines. It is under the ownership of the Government of India and under administrative control of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, with its headquarters in Mumbai.
